title: Frobenius evaluation and open compactification projection squares
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For every finite-type $k_0$-scheme $W_0$ occurring below put $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_W=\operatorname{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_W=Lg_W^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_WK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, with morphisms $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_W(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Give the underlying operations their standard lifts: $H(K,\theta)=(HK,H(\theta)c_{H,K})$, where $c_H:P_{\rm out}H\xrightarrow{\sim}HP_{\rm in}$ is the canonical Frobenius comparison; tensor has structure $(\theta_M\otimes\theta_N)\mu_g$, and internal Hom has structure $R\mathcal Hom(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h_g$. All assertions are restricted to full domains closed under the displayed composites where these operations and comparisons have the stated constructible typing. Retain all underlying finite-Tor, lattice-presentation and witnessed-origin restrictions. No separatedness of the structural morphisms $W_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is imposed.

Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite type, let $f$ be its geometric base change, and choose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the actual maps $\pi_u$, $\gamma$ and $\operatorname{PF}_f^c$ of [def-exchange-projection], and the ordinary adjunctions, tensor comparisons and operation Frobenius structures. Suppose the ordinary adjunction maps and tensor/pullback comparisons are already Weil morphisms; use the canonical exchange and refinement comparisons on their supplied domains. For a scheme $W$ occurring here put $H(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$, and take $M,N$ such that $H(M,N)$ and the displayed tensor are in the stipulated domain. Use the evaluation-defined Hom transport $h:P_WH(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(P_WM,P_WN)$ and tensor transport $\mu$ of [sk-def-sf-operations](i), [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation, lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}:M\otimes^LH(M,N)\to N$. Then
$$\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(\theta_M\otimes H(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h)\mu=\theta_NP_W(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}).$$
Thus evaluation is a Weil morphism, without a new site-perfectness assertion.

The ordinary projection transformation
$$\pi_{u;M,N}=Ru_*((\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1)\mu_{u;Ru_*M,N})\eta_{u,Ru_*M\otimes N}$$
is a Weil morphism on its domain. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ in the compactification, form its pullback $j':U'\hookrightarrow W'$ by the Frobenius base-change isomorphism $t:W'\to W$, with $s:U'\to U$. Use $\beta:Lt^*j_!\simeq j'_!Ls^*$ and $\gamma_{M,N}:j_!M\otimes^LN\simeq j_!(M\otimes^Lj^*N)$ normalized as in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The following equality holds, after inserting the canonical tensor and pullback composition comparisons:
$$j'_!(\mu_s)\,\beta_{M\otimes j^*N}\,Lt^*(\gamma_{M,N})=\gamma'_{Ls^*M,Lt^*N}\,(\beta_M\otimes1)\,\mu_t.$$
It is the equality of maps from $Lt^*(j_!M\otimes N)$ to $j'_!(Ls^*M\otimes j'^*Lt^*N)$. It holds also for the strict inverse coefficient systems, their supplied integral realizations, and their localized/common-stage maps. Consequently the specified open projection comparison and $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c=Rp_*(\gamma_{K,L})\pi_{p;j_!K,L}$ are Weil morphisms, compatible with the supplied compactification refinement comparisons. This asserts equivariance on the original tensor and finite-Tor domains, not new invertibility or constructibility.

For a permitted pair morphism (i inverse opposite,f), precompose Hom-first naturality with tensor(identity,i) and cancel i followed by its inverse; braiding naturality gives tensor(i,H(i inverse,f)) followed by argument-first evaluation = argument-first evaluation followed by f. Specialize to the inverse and forward Weil structures. Factor the tensor map through tensor(identity,kappa), substitute podArgumentFirst_integral_rational or podArgumentFirst_common, and use the supplied component normalizations hP,hT,hH,hSC,hkappa,hmu,hbeta. No separatedness or new domain restriction is used.

proof.text: For open_projection, use the left projectionMap of the supplied lifted open adjunction with the inverse lifted tensor comparison. Its carrier is the original projectionMap: compute the inverse comparison carrier by cancellation against the normalized forward comparison, then substitute the unit and counit carrier equations. The supplied gamma normalization identifies this carrier with gamma inverse. The forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, so invert this Weil arrow. Cancellation identifies its carrier with gamma. For compact_projection apply ordinary_projection to p, compose with the lifted open_projection evaluated at (K,p^*N), and then apply the lifted proper functor. Insert J of tensor(1,phiW) for the supplied pullback compositor. The carrier equations _phi and _gammaP identify the composite exactly with compactificationProjectionFromData. These are categorical supplied-domain statements: the geometric input adjunctions and comparisons are already hypotheses, so no new model compactification is chosen.

proof.text: The refinement statements supply the underlying canonical projection/refinement identity. For refinement_compatibility, faithfulness of IsoAlgebra.forget promotes that identity directly to equality of Weil arrows. For refinement_transport compose rhoS inverse, pf1, and rhoT. Its carrier equals pf2 after substitution of the underlying identity and cancellation of rhoS inverse times rhoS. The IsoAlgebra inverse/composition laws give pf1 followed by rhoT = rhoS followed by the constructed arrow. Only the supplied refinement isomorphisms are inverted. The proof retains all supplied domains and does not require either projection to be invertible.
